title: Central squared-profile deficit
statement:
Let $a,b\in\bbr$ satisfy $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, and $a+b<1$. Writing $Q$ for the lower standard Gaussian quantile and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for the Gaussian density evaluated at that quantile, one has
\[
2Q(a)^2b^2\le I(a+b)^2+I(a-b)^2+2b^2-2I(a)^2.
\]
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. If $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, and $a+b<1$, then $2Q(a)^2b^2\le I(a+b)^2+I(a-b)^2+2b^2-2I(a)^2$.
